meta.title: Launch Your First AI-Assisted Campaign in 5 Steps
meta.subtitle: A practical, repeatable path from idea to live campaign — without boiling the ocean.
meta.author: Sam Whitfield

blocks.alt: A simple campaign workflow on a board
blocks.caption: One narrow, repeatable workflow beats a grand rollout.

blocks.text: You do not need a platform migration to get value from AI. You need one workflow, one honest metric, and the discipline to keep a human in the loop.

items: Pick the single highest-friction step your team dreads most.
Pilot one AI assist on it — variants, lead scoring, or segmentation.
Keep a human approval gate; treat every output as a first draft.
Measure one honest metric, not five vanity ones.
Expand only after the first win is undeniable.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.body: Skipping the approval gate. Speed without review is how off-brand copy reaches production and trust evaporates.

blocks.text: The teams that win start embarrassingly small — and then they do not stop.

blocks.body: Start narrow, keep a human gate, measure one thing honestly. Momentum does the rest.

meta.title: Run a Technical SEO Audit in an Afternoon
meta.subtitle: A focused, repeatable audit that surfaces the issues actually costing you traffic — and skips the busywork.
meta.author: Priya Anand

blocks.caption: Audit the few things that move rankings, not the hundred that do not.

blocks.text: Most SEO audits drown teams in a 200-row checklist nobody finishes. This one focuses on the handful of issues that actually move rankings.

items: Confirm crawlability: robots.txt, sitemaps, and indexation.
Check Core Web Vitals on your top 10 pages.
Find and fix broken internal links and redirect chains.
Audit titles and meta for your highest-traffic templates.
Review structured data on key page types.
Prioritize fixes by traffic-at-risk, then ship the top three.

blocks.code:
# Quick crawl-health check
curl -s https://example.com/robots.txt
curl -sI https://example.com/ | grep -i 'x-robots-tag'

blocks.title: Where teams waste time
blocks.body: Chasing every warning. Sort by traffic-at-risk and fix the top three. The long tail can wait.
A good audit is short and ruthless: crawl, vitals, links, metadata, schema, then ship the three fixes that matter.

meta.title: Migrate to a New CRM Without Losing Your Mind
meta.subtitle: A staged migration plan that keeps the business running while you move — and keeps the data clean when you land.
meta.author: Jordan Park

blocks.caption: Migrate in stages; never big-bang a system the whole company depends on.

blocks.text: A CRM migration fails in the data, not the demo. Plan the move like a renovation you have to live in: in stages, with the lights on the whole time.

items: Freeze scope: list the objects and fields you actually use.
Clean the source data before you move a single record.
Map fields explicitly; document every transform.
Run a dry-run import into a sandbox and reconcile.
Cut over one team first; fix what breaks before scaling.
Retire the old system only after a clean parity week.

blocks.title: The trap
blocks.body: Migrating dirty data. Garbage in, garbage in a more expensive system. Clean first, always.

blocks.text: Nobody remembers a slow migration. Everybody remembers a lossy one.
blocks.source: — Jordan Park, Head of Ops, Tideway

blocks.body: Freeze, clean, map, dry-run, pilot, retire. Staged and boring beats fast and lossy every time.
